title: WPMS/1823/2012 of DR. NARENDRA SWARUP BHATNAGAR Vs PRESCRIBED AUTHORITY AND ORS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 1823 of 2012
Dr. Narendra Swarup Bhatnagar ...Petitioner
Versus
Prescribed Authority/Sub-Divisional Magistrate
(Sadar) Dehradun and others ÖRespondents

Present: Mr. Shashank Pandey, Counsel with Mr. Vikas Bahuguna,
Counsel for the petitioner.
 Mr. R. C. Arya, Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Neeraj Garg, Counsel for respondent no. 3.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. Heard Mr. Shashank Pandey, Counsel with Mr. Vikas
Bahuguna, Counsel for the petitioner, Mr. R. C. Arya,
Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand and
Mr. Neeraj Garg, Counsel for respondent no. 3.
2. The petitioner before this Court has challenged the
order dated 25.5.2012 which has been passed by the
prescribed authority under Section 25 of the Societies
Registration Act, 1860 (hereinafter referred to as the
ìActî) stating that under the circumstances where the
petitioner for the similar cause has filed a civil suit before
the Civil Court it he has no jurisdiction to decide the
election of the management committee. Section 25 of the
Act as it is applicable in the State of Uttarakhand and
Uttar Pradesh reads as under:-
 ì25. Disputes regarding election of
office-bearers.- (1) The prescribed authority
may, on a reference made to it by the Registrar
or by at least one-fourth of the members of a
society registered in Uttar Pradesh, hear and
decide in a summary manner any doubt or
dispute in respect of the election or
continuance in office of an office-bearer of
such society, and may pass such orders in
respect thereof as it deems fit:

2
 [Provided that the election of an office-bearer shall be set aside where the prescribed
authority is satisfied-
 (a) that any corrupt practice has been
committed by such office-bearer; or
 (b) that the nomination of any candidate
has been improperly rejected ; or
 (c) that the result of the election in so far
it concerns such office- bearer has been
materially affected by the improper acceptance
of any nomination or by the improper
reception, refusal or rejection of any vote or
the reception of any vote which is void or by
any non-compliance with the provisions of any
rules of the society.
 Explanation I.- A person shall be deemed
to have committed a corrupt practice who,
directly or indirectly, by himself or by any
other person-
 (i) induces, or attempts to induce, by
fraud, intentional misrepresentation, coercion
or threat of injury, any elector to give or to
refrain from giving a vote in favour of any
candidate, or any person to stand or not to
stand as, or to withdraw or not to withdraw
from being a candidate at the election;
 (ii) with a view to inducing any elector to
give or to refrain from giving a vote in favour of
any candidate, or to inducing any person to
stand or not to stand as, or to withdraw or not
to withdraw from being a candidate at the
election, officers or gives any money, or
valuable consideration, or any place of
employment, or holds out any promise of
individual advantage or profit to any person;
 (iii) abets (within the meaning of the
Indian Penal Code) the doing of any of the acts
specified in clauses (i) and (ii);
 (iv) induces or attempts to induce a
candidate or elector to believe that he, or any
person in whom he is interested, will become
or will be rendered an object of divine
displeasure or spiritual censure;
 (v) canvasses on grounds of caste,
community, sect or religion;
(vi) commits such other practice as the
State Government may prescribe to be a
corrupt practice.
Explanation II.- A ëpromise of individual
advantage or profit to a personí includes a

3
promise for the benefit of the person himself,
or of anyone in whom he is interested.
Explanation III.- The State Government
may prescribe the procedure for hearing and
decision of doubts or disputes in respect of
such elections and make provision in respect
of any other matter relating to such elections
for which insufficient provision exists in this
Act or in the rules of the society.]
(2) Where by an order made under sub-section (1), an election is set aside on an office-bearer is held no longer entitled to continue in
office or where the Registrar is satisfied that
any election of office-bearers of a society has
not been held within the time specified in the
rules of that society, he may call meeting of the
general body of such society for electing such
office-bearer or office-bearers and such
meeting shall be presided over and be
conducted by the Registrar or by any officer
authorized by him in this behalf, and the
provisions in the rules of the society relating to
meetings and elections shall apply to such
meeting and election with necessary
modifications.
(3) Where a meeting is called by the
Registrar under sub-section (2), no other
meeting shall be called for the purpose of
election by any other authority or by any
person claiming to be an office-bearer of the
society.
Explanation.- For the purposes of this
section, the expression ëprescribed authority,
means an officer or court authorized in this
behalf by the State Government by notification
published in the Official Gazette.î

2. The petitioner moved an application before the
Registrar, Firm, Societies and Chits wherein objection
was raised by the present respondent that for the same
cause of action civil suit being Original Suit No. 3 of 2011
is pending before the civil court and therefore in view of
the decision of the Honíble Allahabad High Court in C/M
Sri Manas Shiksha Prasar Samiti and another V. State
of U.P. and others reported in 2011 (29) LCD 2238 in

4
such matters a person cannot avail two remedies at the
same time; one by filing a civil suit and the other before
prescribed authority under Section 25 of the Act.
3. In the said judgment of learned Single Judge of
Honíble Allahabad High Court it has been held that the
remedy lies under Section 25 of the Act for challenging
election of the society, however, this cannot be availed as
for the same cause of action the petitioner has also filed a
suit. In the said case a civil suit as well as an application
was moved under Section 25 of the Act for the same
cause of action and the only reason assigned by the
concerned person before the Honíble High Court was that
civil suit has been filed as the prescribed authority does
not have powers to grant injunction. Whereas before this
Court it has clearly been contended by the petitioner that
the suit filed by him before the civil court is for entirely
different relief! In the suit what has been prayed is that
the management committee be restrained from calling
any further meeting as it is not properly constituted
management committee inasmuch as the representative
of foundersí family has no representation in the
management committee. This is the entire basis of the
filing of the civil suit. Whereas in the application under
Section 25 of the Act the petitioner has challenged the
entire election of the management committee held on
28.11.2010. These submissions of the learned counsel
for the petitioner appear to be correct. Therefore in
substance the two remedies are entirely different
remedies and therefore decision of the prescribed
authority that it has no jurisdiction in the matter based
on the Honíble Allahabad High Court judgment is
patently erroneous and based on a misreading of law.

5
4. The writ petition is therefore allowed. The order
dated 25.5.2012 is hereby set aside. The prescribed
authority is hereby directed to decide the reference, as
expeditiously as possible but definitely within a period of
three months from the date a certified copy of this order
is produced before him.
5. No order as to costs.
